tasks.subject: T1: Proxy alias — body fingerprint + loud unresolvable-alias failure
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Fold `_fingerprint_function(func)` into `_stable_cfunc_alias`'s raw key so same-identity different-body proxies (factory same-qualname closures, in-process redefinition, fork twins on a shared cache) get distinct aliases instead of silently reaching the wrong body via last-writer-wins `add_symbol` (H2, M9). Make an absent binding whose alias is referenced by a warm cache=True caller fail loudly instead of a bare SIGSEGV (H1).

**Files:** `numbox/core/proxy/proxy.py`, `test/core/test_proxy.py`, `docs/numbox.core.proxy.rst`.

**Outcome / design notes:** (1) Fold done — factory closures + redefinition now dispatch to their own body (H2/M9 repros pass). An adversarial-verify pass caught that the first fold was INCOMPLETE for numbox's own idiom: every binding body calls the @intrinsic _call_lib_func, so _fingerprint_function bailed to a bytecode-only fallback blind to constants/closures and a factory over different C symbol names still collided; fixed with _fingerprint_function_best_effort (lenient, never-raises, captures consts/closure/defaults/globals with opaque placeholders), process-stable, with a cos/sin factory regression test. (2) Loud failure for the availability-flip (H1): `proxy_if_available`'s absent path registers a cfunc trap under the would-be alias (`_register_absent_alias_trap`); the warm caller resolves it and gets a named RuntimeError on stderr, not a SIGSEGV. (3) An `extern_weak` + null-check IR guard was tried and REJECTED — it does not survive numba's object-code cache reload (the undefined-weak address materializes via a PC-relative relocation to non-null garbage, so the null-check passes and the call still segfaults; proven with faulthandler). (4) Signature/body change renames the alias while the binding is present, which no runtime guard can catch; documented as a cache-clear requirement (M10 + the body-edit case the fold introduces), matching M10's verdict (medium, upgrade-time, existing doc precedent). Codegen refactored into `_call_proxied_alias` so the exec'd template shrank (the co_firstlineno anchor minimum dropped, not rose).

tasks.subject: T2: Route shallow keys through the deep walker + enrich _canon_value
tasks.description:
**OUTCOME (5 sub-commits):** H3 needed MORE than the review's stated fix (the derive's own standalone numba cache is the staleness source, not the kernel name) -- state-reading derives are now compiled uncached + fingerprinted (2ea650e). H4: method hash folds the deep fingerprint + referenced ns values so the content-addressed anchor changes when behaviour does (7e5de2f). H7/M11/L23: digest fallback routes un-fingerprintable FUNCTIONS through the best-effort walker (captures closure/consts, sorts sets -> PYTHONHASHSEED-stable); cloudpickle kept only for codeless callables, confining L23's uuid4 residual there (c2da184). H8: the walker identifies a @proxy binding by its stable alias (proxy tag + _canon_value short-circuit) so sqlite callbacks fingerprint cleanly + distinctly (56cbc6c). L21: structured-dtype ndarrays canonicalize by full descriptor+itemsize, not dtype.str=|Vn. L22: UDAF digest subject folds the state type's module+qualname. Regression tests: test_cache_crossprocess.py (H3, H4, M11 -- each fails pre-fix, passes post), test_fingerprint.py (H8, L21), test_digest.py (H7). Full suite green.

**Goal:** Make the source-text-only / bare-code keys use the closure/global-aware walker, degrading to uncached on `_Unfingerprintable` like `compile_kernel`.

- `builder.py` derive hashing: `_fingerprint_function(derive)` instead of `sha256(getsource)`; catch `OSError` from `getsource` (exec/REPL derives) and `_Unfingerprintable` -> uncached, never crash (H3, L19).
- `make_structref` (`highlevel.py`): walk the method functions so `ns`-threaded values enter the key (H4).
- `digest()` fallback (`digest.py`): cloudpickle the function *object* (captures closure/defaults), sort where iteration order leaks (H7, M11, L23).
- sqlite UDAF/TVF (`udf_helpers.py`, `tvf.py`): teach the walker the proxy-wrapper shape so realistic `sqlite3_value_*`/`sqlite3_result_*` callbacks fingerprint cleanly instead of degrading (H8).
- `_canon_value` (`fingerprint.py`): structured-dtype ndarrays by full layout not `dtype.str` (L21); StructRef identity includes module + `@overload_method` behavior (L22).

**Files:** `numbox/core/work/builder.py`, `numbox/utils/highlevel.py`, `numbox/utils/digest.py`, `numbox/utils/fingerprint.py`, `numbox/core/bindings/sqlite/udf_helpers.py`, `numbox/core/bindings/sqlite/tvf.py`, `numbox/utils/preprocessing.py`, tests.

**Note:** the largest task — commit in two parts if cleaner (walker enrichments + degrade helper, then the four consumers). Adversarial verify.

Need BOTH (a) fold _effective_flags(jit_options) into _kernel_fingerprint so _make_<hash> re-keys, and (b) give the derive a flag-dependent cache identity via a digest-named _derive_<digest> anchor-wrapper (digest folds derive fingerprint + effective flags), njit'd with the flags, cache=True, anchored -- mirroring compile_kernel._compile (whose traps are now known). builder already handles reads_module_state->uncacheable and the exec/REPL locator fallback.
